original_test_intent: Read the active ROT firmware record from the correct verified BMC and prove its uniquely identified version matches the authoritative GPU firmware/software release mapping.
original_method: Authenticate through an approved read-only broker with TLS verification, retrieve the exact ROT active resource, retain redacted response/status/audit evidence, extract the active version and compare it with the supplied release baseline.
manual_activity: Engineer/security supplies trusted endpoint, credential and expected version mapping, reviews mismatch/security anomalies and decides the DUT verdict.
required_inputs: Verified BMC address, Redfish service identity and TLS CA/certificate
Expected ROT version and authoritative release note
Read-only credential broker/account role and network ACL
Redaction, audit and protected evidence policy
safety_requirements: Verify host/certificate and target identity before credentials
Query only the exact inventory resource and no actions
Redact tokens, secrets and unrelated inventory
agent_execution_scope: Capture allowed status/headers/redacted JSON and audit timestamps
Extract unique active ROT version and compare to supplied baseline
Do not use insecure flags, query update actions or decide PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve endpoint/trust/credential and ROT component mapping
Resolve response/version/security discrepancies and decide PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Broad insecure inventory access can select the wrong component and exposes credentials; it is not acceptable evidence for the exact ROT active resource.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: TLS-verify the approved BMC and GET the exact ROT active Redfish resource using brokered read-only credentials, then compare the uniquely mapped version.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: ROT active inventory intent, release-note comparison and source 5/5 timing are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record a minimal redacted evidence bundle binding BMC identity, resource URI, component ID, active-state/version and release-note baseline.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Secures transport and identity without changing the read-only check.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Broad inventory or another firmware component does not satisfy ROT.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Vendor Redfish schemas may encode version fields differently; the approved component/schema mapping must be versioned.

project_override_considerations: Project authority may approve an equivalent secure SMC query only if it uniquely identifies active ROT and maps to the same release baseline; no firmware mutation is implied.
expected_evidence: Exact resource URI, HTTP status, timestamp and redacted JSON
BMC audit/security anomalies and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, exact rot_active URI and Criteria consistently target active ROT version; insecure historical access is an implementation defect rather than competing coverage.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Endpoint, trust, credential and expected mapping can be supplied; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Moves from insecure broad inventory access to a TLS-verified, uniquely identified and release-mapped ROT active record with minimal redacted evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Firmware inventory can contain staged, backup and similarly named devices; a version string is meaningful only when bound to the correct BMC, exact component identity and active state. TLS and secure credentials also protect the evidence path from substitution. A broad response can look plausible while proving the wrong firmware.
